topic: Two siblings inherit their grandmother's house
text: When Grandma's will was read, I found myself standing there with my sister, the house keys between us. It's a beautiful old place, filled with memories and her touch in every corner. My sister suggested we sell it, divide the money, and be done. Part of me understands her practicality, but the idea gnaws at me. Selling feels like closing a chapter before I've had a chance to read it one last time. Maybe we could keep it, visit occasionally, and hold on to a piece of her that way. I just can't shake the thought that rushing to sell it would be a quick fix for something that needs more time and care.
